newsitem.title: UK: EMI, HTV and YTV team up in lottery cash bid.
newsitem.headline: EMI, HTV and YTV team up in lottery cash bid.

text.p: A consortium featuring Elton John's Rocket Pictures, EMI Music Publishing plus HTV and Yorkshire Tyne-Tees Television is seeking UK lottery cash for a film production venture.

The four have joined forces with Partners In Film, a grouping of four film finance, production and distribution companies, to apply for one of four franchises to be awarded by the Arts Council of England.

The Arts Council will award up to 39 million pounds of national lottery funding under each of the six-year franchises. The deadline for applications is the end of the month and the awards are expected to be announced at the end of May.
The consortium plans to produce 34 British feature films over the term of the franchise. Budgets will average 5.3 million pounds, giving a total investment of 179 million.
The other partners in the consortium are Merchant Ivory Production, Capitol Films, First Independent Films and merchant bank Guinness Mahon.

Rocket Pictures, HTV's Harvest Entertainment and Yorkshire's Griffin Productions plan to route their lottery-eligible films through the company, while EMI Music will finance projects in exchange for soundtrack rights.
The Arts Council has previously used lottery money to fund one-off film productions but aims now to give the British industry a more permanent base on which to build.
